Abstract: Smartphone and wearable device such a smartwatch have become part of everyday life offer person convenient acces to personal health and digital service Some emerge system use heartbased biometric signal capture through photoplethysmography PPG sensor in these device to authenticate user continuously without require password or active interaction This seamless unobtrusive form of authentication can enhance both security and user experience However PPGbased continuous authentication also introduce new privacy and cybersecurity risk if attacker can fool the system In particular biometric system can be subject to impersonation attack where an attacker try to present signal that mimic a target user This project explore the risk of presentation attack in PPGbased biometric system in which an adversary capture a person heart signal via video and replay a synthetic version tailor for a target device to impersonate the user The project team also explore defense mechanism that identify unique characteristic of signal from real human user that be difficult to reproduce synthetically By examine this practical attack and develop a target defense the research aim to reduce impersonation risk build trust in biometric authentication and support the broad adoption of PPGbased authentication system in securitysensitive application The project also contribute to national priority in cybersecurity STEM education and workforce development through student mentor curriculum integration and outreach to local school and community This project examine the feasibility of presentation attack on PPGbased continuous authentication system use in mobile and wearable device and develop practical method for defend against it The research include four coordinate component First the investigator will study how cardiac signal can be acquire remotely use videobased remote PPG sense under realistic covert record condition This component apply datadriven enhancement technique to reduce the impact of motion and light variation improve signal quality for adversarial use Second the project will develop a deep learning framework to transform remotely captured signal into synthetic waveform that closely resemble those generate by contact PPG sensor in the wearable and mobile device Domain adaptation technique will be investigate to ensure the model generalize across different device configuration while reduce retrain effort Third the team will design a physical signal injection method that use a controllable external light source guide by a learned model of sensor response to deliver spoofed signal to the target device PPG sensor This method be intend to operate without modify the device hardware or software enable a loweffort and covert attack pathway Finally the researcher will develop a hybrid livenes detection system that distinguish genuine cardiac signal from synthetic one by identify subtle physiological feature that be difficult to reproduce Adaptive learning strategy will be incorporate to address natural variability in heart signal enhance detection reliability over time Project outcome will include curated dataset hardware
